continuity_scope: Guild Wars 2: End of Dragons expansion launch campaign as released on 28 February 2022, bounded to ArenaNet's 7 April 2022 official post-campaign Aetherblades narrative case study. It is a Guild Wars 2 live-service expansion pass, not a Guild Wars (2005)/Guild Wars 1 pass and not a record of Living World, Heart of Thorns, Path of Fire, Icebrood Saga, Secrets of the Obscure, later End of Dragons 2023 chapters, patches, or future game eras.
work_or_witnesses: ArenaNet, Guild Wars 2: End of Dragons is Live, 28 February 2022
ArenaNet, Developing the Aetherblades, 7 April 2022, explicit post-campaign spoiler warning
ArenaNet, Guild Wars 2 in 2023, later End of Dragons story-update boundary only
ArenaNet, A New Chapter Begins in Guild Wars 2: Secrets of the Obscure, post-Dragon-Cycle/live-service-era boundary only
coverage_rule: All stable named NPC dramatic individuals directly given a concrete End of Dragons narrative role in the selected official Aetherblades case study: Ankka, Mai Trin, Joon, Scarlet, and Ivan. The article expressly frames Ankka and Mai as extended design case studies, identifies Joon and Scarlet as the contrasting inventor/mentor and former-leader forces in Mai's arc, and gives Ivan a named legacy role. The player-created Commander/avatar is not a character node. Other names occur only as historical references, developer/actor credits, generic player roles, or unprofiled contextual mentions and are excluded.
omissions: The player-created Commander/avatar and every player-specific race, appearance, profession, biography choice, build, order, dialogue selection, personal-story branch, and achievement state.

Named figures not directly given an End of Dragons Aetherblades-plot role in the selected article, including contextual historical references, NPCs from other campaigns, and all generic Aetherblades, factions, dragons, species, professions, items, regions, masteries, and mechanics as character nodes.

Guild Wars (2005) and its campaigns/expansions; Guild Wars 2 core game, Living World, Heart of Thorns, Path of Fire, Icebrood Saga, later 2023 End of Dragons maps/story chapters, Secrets of the Obscure and subsequent releases, adaptations, fan wikis, Wikipedia, walkthroughs, and community databases.
uncertainties: The selected official source is a retrospective developer narrative article, not an exhaustive in-game journal or cast directory. Completion applies only to its stated five-person Aetherblades case-study rule.

The article contains explicit End of Dragons spoilers and discusses material from older Guild Wars 2 releases as backstory. Those older events are not silently made part of this launch-campaign continuity; only their direct relevance as this article states it is recorded.
ArenaNet's own article says opinions about whether Mai Trin is redeemed by her sacrifice are deliberately non-universal. No moral verdict is normalized.

Live-service content continues after launch: ArenaNet announced a new End of Dragons map/story chapter for February 2023 and later marked Secrets of the Obscure as a new post-Dragon-Cycle chapter. Neither is in scope.
The English ArenaNet web witness is used as an English presentation. It does not establish identity of wording, voice performance, or text in every localization or patch.
evidence_basis: Official ArenaNet Guild Wars 2 expansion-launch and narrative-development pages. The character claims are constrained to direct statements in the signed Story Design Lead post; no fan wiki, Wikipedia, walkthrough, or database is used as canonical evidence.
